text:
ria: quick heads-up — p95 dashboard render latency spiked yesterday. flame graphs point to auth checks executed deep inside service joins. thinking about an "auth-hint" header from the gateway that tells downstreams an allowed-column set + cheap row-mask to short-circuit heavy work.

omar: can you sketch the hint payload? would it be a proto or just a small JSON blob?

ria: small stable proto. idea: gateway performs a batched, lightweight policy eval that produces a compact hint: {etag, columns_mask, row_mask_expr, strict_mode:false}. downstreams can apply row_mask_expr as a DB predicate or use columns_mask to prune projection. if hint is missing/mismatch, fall back to normal policy call.

tali: huge win if it cuts N auth calls per widget. but we must avoid unsafe optimistic hints. proposal: hint is advisory unless strict_mode=true and only after rollout. default to advisory.

kevin: ops concerns: more metadata on the wire, new gateway CPU load, cache coherency. what's the expected size and TTL?

ria: estimate 200-800 bytes per hint depending on mask encoding. TTL 30s by default for active sessions; invalidation hooks on role/seat changes. gateway caches per request token short-term for batching.

omar: correctness: two failure classes: 1) stale hint under-restricts — dangerous; 2) stale hint over-restricts — annoying but safe. always favor safety: hint must never broaden permission. runtime rule: apply hint only if it is a subset of what full policy returns, else ignore. during rollout run in audit mode where we attach hint but still perform full-policy for sampled requests and log divergences.

kevin: rollout plan suggestion: 1) implement hint service + gateway integration behind flag; 2) stage in audit mode with 5% sampling of double-checks for 72h; 3) raise sample to 100% for small tenant cohort for 48h; 4) flip strict_mode for single-tenant dashboards; keep multi-tenant off. include kill-switch.

yara: metrics to add: hint.latency_ms, hint.cache_hit_rate, hint.divergence_count, hint.size_bytes, downstream.render_saved_work_ms. also trace link between hint.apply=true and DB read bytes saved.

tali: how to apply in SQL services? options: gateway can also attach an optimized WHERE fragment (SQL-safe). but DB-level injection must be sanitized. maybe return a canonical AST rather than raw SQL to avoid injection risk.

omar: AST approach safer but adds parser/compile work in services. compromise: return a paramized predicate + params list. example: {predicate: "tenant_id = ? AND status != ?", params: [42, "archived"]}. services can map params to typed query builders.

ria: good call. also implement an ETag so downstream caches per (etag, subject, resource). downstreams can short-circuit if cached etag matches. invalidation via write-hooks (role change, seat revoke) will bump etag.

kevin: infra sizing: gateway will need small but fast instances; hint service CPU-bound but low memory. batch endpoint critical to lower p95. recommend connection pooling and keepalive.

yara: alerting: hint.divergence.rate > 0.1% sustained 1h, hint.latency.p95 > 40ms, hint.error_rate > 0.5% tenant. playbook: disable gateway flag, purge caches, rollback hint service.

omar: testing: unit tests for predicate correctness, integration tests with synthetic dashboards, stress tests for batch sizes. also chaos test: simulate write invalidation during heavy reads.

tali: owners: ria (design + RFC), omar (policy correctness + tests), kevin (ops + deployment), yara (telemetry). I'll also volunteer to implement downstream cache library for SQL services.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary queued for branch "auth-hint-proto" to staging. ETA ~20m.

ria: thanks — i'll draft short RFC with payload proto, TTL, rollout steps, and the conservative semantics. meeting Friday to review. :rocket:
